chunks: And by this chain, from Abaan ibn Uthman, from Ismail al-Basri, who said:

I heard Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) saying: 'You sit in a place, narrate (hadith), and say whatever you wish, and distance yourselves from whomever you wish, and befriend whomever you wish.' I said, 'Yes.' He said: 'Is life (luxury) anything other than this?'

key_terms.الْعَيْشُ: Life, livelihood, or the luxury of living
key_terms.تَتَبَّرَءُونَ: To distance oneself or declare disassociation from someone
key_terms.تَوَلَّوْنَ: To befriend or show allegiance to someone

ai.seo_question: What does Imam al-Sadiq say constitutes the essence of a good life for scholars?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) characterizes the life of the scholars and narrators as one of intellectual autonomy, where they sit in their places to transmit traditions while exercising independent judgment in declaring allegiance and disavowal (Tawalla and Tabarra). He concludes that this freedom of discourse and doctrinal independence constitutes the very essence of a good and dignified life (al-'ishr). This highlights the Shia scholarly tradition's emphasis on the narrator's authority to interpret and apply religious principles without rigid external constraint.

en.hubeali: H 14740 – And by this chain, from Abaan Bin Usman, from Ismail Al-Basary who said:

I heard Abu Abdullahasws saying: ‘Can you all sit in a place where you can narrate Hadith, say whatsoever you like, and distance yourselves (Tabarra) from whosoever you like, and befriend whosoever you like?’ I said, ‘Yes’. Heasws said: ‘Is (luxury of) life anything other than this?’
